summary.grade_trigger: Automatic F — confirmed breach of 2 critical red-team objectives

findings.title: Complete Absence of Authentication & Authorization
findings.owasp: A01: Broken Access Control, A07: Identification and Authentication Failures
findings.description: Every API endpoint — including all state-changing operations (approve, reject, dispatch, delete) — is reachable by any anonymous HTTP caller. No JWT, session, API-key, or IP-restriction middleware exists at any layer. RED-001 confirmed: anonymous GET /api/work-items returned HTTP 200; anonymous POST /api/work-items returned HTTP 201. This is the universal enabler for all other confirmed exploits.
findings.remediation: Add authentication middleware (JWT bearer or API-key) before all /api/* routes in app.ts. This is the single highest-priority fix — without it, all other mitigations are trivially bypassed.

findings.title: Fast-Track Override Bypasses State Machine — Critical Objective Achieved
findings.owasp: A01: Broken Access Control, A04: Insecure Design
findings.description: POST /api/work-items/:id/route accepts overrideRoute:"fast-track" in the request body with no privilege gate. RED-002 confirmed: 3 unauthenticated HTTP calls (create → route with fast-track → dispatch) moved a work item from backlog to in-progress with an empty assessments array. Red-team objective ACHIEVED: 'Bypass work item state machine to reach an invalid status.'
findings.remediation: Remove overrideRoute from the public API entirely. If internal fast-track is needed, gate it behind an admin role/scope and validate the value against Object.values(WorkItemRoute).

findings.title: Direct /approve Endpoint Bypasses Mandatory Assessment Pod
findings.owasp: A01: Broken Access Control, A04: Insecure Design
findings.description: POST /api/work-items/:id/approve allows a Proposed item to be approved without running the assessment pod. RED-003 confirmed: create → route (full-review) → approve directly → item approved with empty assessments[] and no reviewing entry in changeHistory.
findings.remediation: Gate /approve behind an assessment precondition: require assessments.length >= 4 (one per required role) before allowing approval. Alternatively, remove the manual approve endpoint and only permit approval through the automated assessment pod.

findings.title: Unlimited Pagination — Full Dataset Enumeration — Objective Achieved
findings.description: GET /api/work-items and GET /api/dashboard/activity accept limit as a query parameter with no maximum cap. RED-004 confirmed: limit=9999999 returned all 8 items in a single response with data.length == total. Also confirmed: limit=-1 returns N-1 items (off-by-one via slice behavior). Red-team objective ACHIEVED: 'Enumerate all work items without pagination limit enforcement.'
findings.remediation: Add MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 100 constant. Enforce: limit = Math.min(Math.max(1, parseInt(limit) || 20), MAX_PAGE_SIZE). Return 400 for non-positive or non-numeric values.

findings.title: Cascade Auto-Dispatch Hijack via Reject
findings.description: POST /api/work-items/:id/reject triggers onItemResolved(), which auto-dispatches all Approved dependents to InProgress without going through the /dispatch endpoint or team allowlist validation. RED-006 confirmed: rejecting item A auto-dispatched dependents B and C to in-progress (Prometheus metric: dispatch_gating_events_total{event='cascade_dispatched'} 2).
findings.remediation: Remove automatic cascade dispatch from onItemResolved. It should only unblock items (remove the blocker link), never auto-dispatch. Dispatch must always be an explicit action through the /dispatch endpoint.

findings.title: Intake Webhooks — No Auth, No Signature Verification, Enum Injection
findings.owasp: A07: Identification and Authentication Failures, A03: Injection
findings.description: Both /api/intake/zendesk and /api/intake/automated accept unauthenticated POSTs with no HMAC signature check and no enum validation. RED-007 confirmed: items created with type:'MALICIOUS_VALUE' stored verbatim (HTTP 201). Items WI-016 and WI-017 visible in store dump with invalid enum values. No X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature header required.
findings.remediation: (1) Implement HMAC-SHA256 signature verification using ZENDESK_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var. (2) Add enum validation matching POST /api/work-items. (3) Require API key or IP allowlist for /api/intake/*.

findings.title: Ghost Blocker Permanent DoS via Soft-Delete
findings.description: computeHasUnresolvedBlockers treats a missing (soft-deleted) blocker as unresolved, permanently preventing dispatch of dependents. RED-005 confirmed: soft-deleting item C made dependent D permanently undispatchable (HTTP 400 on dispatch with unresolvedBlockers exposing the deleted item's UUID). Can be weaponized offensively: create dependency, delete blocker, block legitimate work item forever.
findings.remediation: (1) Treat findById returning undefined as 'blocker resolved'. (2) On soft-delete, cascade-remove all dependency links where the item is a blocker.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Security Headers — No helmet Middleware
findings.description: No helmet or security headers are set. Absent: Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, Strict-Transport-Security, Permissions-Policy. X-Powered-By: Express is being sent, advertising the framework version. 6 ASVS L2 controls fail on this finding alone.
findings.remediation: npm install helmet && add app.use(helmet()) as the first middleware in app.ts. Configure CSP to disallow eval and restrict origins. Quickest win: 5-minute fix unlocks 6 compliance controls.

findings.title: No Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) — Principle of Least Privilege Absent
findings.description: Once authentication is added (SEC-001), there is still no RBAC layer. Any authenticated caller can approve, reject, dispatch, or delete. A Zendesk webhook should not be able to approve items; a viewer should not be able to dispatch. The trackUpdates service hardcodes 'user' as the agent string, losing actor identity entirely.
findings.remediation: Define roles (viewer, editor, approver, admin, service-account). Apply role-guard middleware per route. Emit permission_denied audit events on rejection. Capture actual actor identity in all state-change events.

findings.title: Required Compliance Audit Events Absent from Logging Layer
findings.description: All 4 required_audit_events from security.config.yml are missing: login_attempt (no auth layer), permission_denied (no authz layer), state_transition (operational logs exist but lack event_type/actor/outcome fields), data_export (no export feature). Current logger.info calls serve observability, not compliance audit trails.
findings.remediation: Create a dedicated auditLogger module emitting structured events with: event_type, actor, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, timestamp. Wire state_transition events into every workflow state change. Ensure audit logs ship to an immutable sink.

findings.title: Prometheus /metrics Endpoint Unauthenticated — Operational Intelligence Exposed
findings.description: GET /metrics returns full Prometheus exposition with no auth. RED-008 confirmed: full metric output including workflow_items_created_total{source='zendesk',type='MALICIOUS_VALUE'} 1 and dispatch_gating_events_total{event='cascade_dispatched'} 2 — providing a full trace of red-team activity.
findings.remediation: Restrict /metrics to localhost binding or bearer token (METRICS_BEARER_TOKEN env var), or serve on a separate internal-only port (e.g., 9091).

findings.title: No Rate Limiting — Flooding and Memory Exhaustion Risk
findings.description: No express-rate-limit or equivalent middleware. Combined with missing authentication, any caller can flood intake endpoints to exhaust Node.js heap. GET /api/dashboard/activity performs O(N×H) sort over all items' changeHistory — degrading with scale.
findings.remediation: npm install express-rate-limit. Apply global limiter (100 req/min per IP) with tighter limit on intake and mutation endpoints (20 req/min).

findings.title: No CORS Allowlist Policy — Permissive Cross-Origin Behaviour
findings.description: The cors package is absent and no CORS headers are set. Browser defaults may permit cross-origin reads from attacker-controlled pages since no authentication protects the data.
findings.remediation: npm install cors. Configure explicit allowlist: origin: ['http://localhost:5173', 'https://<production-domain>']. Deny credentials sharing until authentication is implemented.

findings.title: TLS/HTTPS Not Enforced at Application Layer
findings.description: No TLS configuration in Express. Vite proxy uses plain http://localhost:3001. No Strict-Transport-Security header. In production, all browser→frontend→backend traffic would be unencrypted unless a reverse proxy is configured externally.
findings.remediation: Add HSTS via helmet (see SEC-008). Document TLS termination boundary in CLAUDE.md. Ensure VITE_API_BASE_URL in production build points to https:// origin.

findings.title: No Encryption-at-Rest Plan for Future Persistence Layer
findings.description: All data is in-memory (Map). No persistence layer today, but any migration to disk would land without encryption controls unless planned now. Currently all data is lost on process restart.
findings.remediation: Before adding persistence: require database-level encryption (PostgreSQL TDE or AES-256-CBC column encryption for sensitive fields) as a migration acceptance criterion. Document in Specifications/ as an architecture decision record.

findings.title: Internal Error Messages Exposed to HTTP Clients
findings.description: Route-level catch blocks return raw err.message directly to HTTP clients, bypassing the global errorHandler. RED-009 confirmed: self-reference dependency returns 'A work item cannot depend on itself (self-reference)'; non-existent UUID reveals store key format; invalid transition exposes the full valid transition map.
findings.remediation: Replace per-route catch blocks to log full error internally and return generic { error: 'Internal server error' } for unexpected 500-level errors. Only 4xx business-rule rejections should include descriptive messages.

findings.title: DebugPortalPage iframe Lacks sandbox Attribute
findings.description: The iframe has no sandbox attribute, granting embedded content the same origin permissions as the parent page. Default URL uses http://. If VITE_PORTAL_URL is misconfigured to an attacker-controlled URL, the embedded content can execute scripts and access the parent DOM.
findings.remediation: Add sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin" to the iframe. Validate VITE_PORTAL_URL to only allow trusted origins.

findings.title: No GDPR Hard-Delete / Right to Erasure Endpoint
findings.description: DELETE /api/work-items/:id performs soft-delete only (item.deleted = true). No purge/hard-delete endpoint. Future PII fields (createdBy, assignee.email) would have no compliant erasure path.
findings.remediation: Implement POST /api/work-items/:id/purge (admin-role only) that physically removes the record. Define data retention schedule and erasure SLA.

findings.title: Stack Traces Logged at Error Level — Filesystem Path Leakage
findings.description: logger.error logs full stack traces (including absolute server filesystem paths like /workspace/Source/Backend/src/...) at ERROR level unconditionally. In environments where logs are shipped to a broadly-accessible aggregator, this constitutes path disclosure.
findings.remediation: Log stack traces at DEBUG level only (behind LOG_LEVEL=debug gate). At ERROR level, log only err.message. Consider a log-scrubbing middleware in production.
